Promoting Academic Integrity in the Context of AI As AI technologies continue to develop, faculty may wish to consider the following strategies: Clearly communicate course and assignment expectations regarding AI use, including whether use is permitted, restricted, or prohibited. Discuss appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI within the context of your discipline and course learning objectives. Design assignments that require students to demonstrate their own learning, reasoning, analysis, and application of course concepts. Consider incorporating drafts, reflections, process documentation, in-class work, presentations, or other opportunities for students to demonstrate how they arrived at their final product. When concerns arise, consider discussing the student's work and process with them as part of gathering relevant information. No single strategy will eliminate academic misconduct.

units.policy: Assignments that allow or call for GAI use are expressly listed as such.

units.passage: With this flexibility, instructors should make sure to clarify to students on what is acceptable and unacceptable use of such tools and systems in their syllabus and assignments.
units.policy: Instructors should make sure to clarify to students what is acceptable and unacceptable use of GAI tools and systems in their syllabus and assignments.
units.why: Instructors 'should make sure to clarify to students on what is acceptable and unacceptable use... in their syllabus and assignments' requires the AI statement in syllabus and assignments, P09.

units.policy: The key issue is being clear and transparent with students about your stance on AI for use in the course.
units.why: 'The key issue is being clear and transparent with students about your stance on AI' repeats the communication expectation; coded P09.

units.passage: These standards and procedures should address the limits of permissible GAI use (including attributing and/or citing GAI tools, if appropriate) and should be carefully articulated in class and the syllabus
units.policy: Faculty standards and procedures for GAI use should address the limits of permissible GAI use and should be carefully articulated in class and the syllabus
units.why: Faculty standards "should address the limits of permissible GAI use" and be "carefully articulated in class and the syllabus", which asks instructors to communicate in the syllabus (P09). The attribution clause is coded separately.

units.passage: Your faculty should include a syllabus statement indicating what is allowed and what is not allowed.
units.why: 'Your faculty should include a syllabus statement indicating what is allowed and what is not allowed' is a recommendation that instructors state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09); actor is instructor, should.

units.passage: Faculty are asked to provide guidance to students via the course syllabus
units.why: 'Faculty are asked to provide guidance to students via the course syllabus and to discuss their expectations in class' asks instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09); 'asked' read as should.

units.passage: and to discuss their expectations in class.
units.why: "and to discuss their expectations in class" asks instructors to talk through expectations; P09 (communicating expectations) is the nearest type and P10 does not apply since it concerns students asking.

units.passage: We recommend starting with this language and adding more specific information for your class.
units.why: 'We recommend starting with this language and adding more specific information for your class' recommends adapting the template into the syllabus; syllabus-statement communication (P09), not tiers (P05).

units.passage: Rather than rely on detection software, MIT suggests that faculty have transparent dialogues about AI use, foster intrinsic motivation, and create inclusive classrooms that support student engagement.
units.why: 'MIT suggests that faculty have transparent dialogues about AI use' recommends instructors openly discuss expectations with students; nearest is P09 (communicate expectations), should.

units.passage: Instructors at the University may allow or prohibit the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools in their courses and are strongly encouraged to include a clear syllabus statement outlining their expectations.
units.why: Instructors are "strongly encouraged to include a clear syllabus statement", which asks for an AI statement in the syllabus (P09); "strongly encouraged" makes it should rather than must.

units.passage: A well-crafted course policy should define acceptable and unacceptable uses of GenAI, reference relevant academic policies, and support students in reaching compliance.
units.policy: A well-crafted course policy defines acceptable and unacceptable uses of GenAI, references relevant academic policies, and supports students in reaching compliance.
units.why: This says what a course policy "should define", i.e. the content of the syllabus AI statement, so P09 fits better than P04 because it does not say who decides.

units.passage: Provide specific examples of how students may or may not use GenAI tools. For example, you may limit AI to specific tasks or assignments.
units.why: Instructors are told to "Provide specific examples" of allowed and disallowed use, which is content of the syllabus statement (P09).

units.passage: Clearly state whether UMN-licensed Generative AI tools are permitted in the course, even if GenAI use is prohibited. Specify which, if any, tools may be used.
units.why: Instructors must "Clearly state" whether licensed tools are allowed, even under a ban. This is a syllabus statement requirement (P09); P17 is for providing a tool, which this does not do.
units.fit_note: Specifically requires a tool-by-tool statement, including when other GenAI use is prohibited. / Specifically about stating which AI tools (esp. UMN-licensed ones) are allowed, even under a ban.

units.passage: Instructors are expected to provide clear standards regarding academic work expectations in the course syllabus.
units.why: The Plagiarism clause quoted for attribution says instructors "are expected to provide clear standards" in the syllabus, a syllabus-statement duty (P09). Final codes after reconciliation: actor=instructor, phase=course-start, modality=must, policy_type=P09, unit_stance=neutral.

units.passage: Example syllabus statements on the use of AI in academic classes, developed by the Senate Committee on Educational Policy
units.why: "Example syllabus statements on the use of AI in academic classes, developed by the Senate Committee on Educational Policy" points instructors to sample statements: P09 is nearest.
units.fit_note: A pointer to example statements; no rule. / Resource link offering sample statements; it does not itself require a syllabus statement.

units.passage: Faculty are encouraged to address guidelines for generative AI tools early in the semester both in the syllabus and in person.
units.why: Faculty "are encouraged to address guidelines ... early in the semester both in the syllabus and in person", a syllabus-statement expectation (P09).

units.passage: Guidelines about appropriate use should be included in the syllabus for each class.
